topic: sub:11|Formulas and equations|Calculate and interpret BAC with the BAC formulas

parts.latex:
Jon has a mass of 84 kg. He was at a friend's party and consumed six bottles of an alcoholic beverage, each equivalent to 0.9 standard drinks.

Blood alcohol content ($BAC$) is calculated using the following formula:

$$BAC_{Male} = \dfrac{10N - 7.5H}{6.8M}$$

where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours of drinking, and $M$ is the person's weight in kilograms.

Jon stopped drinking at 10:30 pm and left the party at 2:30 am, just when his Blood Alcohol Content ($BAC$) reached zero.

The time needed for $BAC$ to reach zero after the last drink consumed can be calculated using the formula:

$$\text{Number of hours for } BAC \text{ to reach zero} = \dfrac{BAC}{0.015}$$

At what time did Jon start to have his first drink at the party? Give your answer to the nearest minute.

solutions.latex:
The time for $BAC$ to reach zero is the time from the last drink (10:30 pm) to 2:30 am, which is $4$ hours. Use the given formula.
$$4 = \dfrac{BAC}{0.015}$$
$$BAC = 0.06$$
The number of standard drinks is $N = 6 \times 0.9 = 5.4$. Substitute into the $BAC$ formula with $M = 84$.
$$0.06 = \dfrac{10 \times 5.4 - 7.5H}{6.8 \times 84}$$
$$H = 2 \text{ h } 38 \text{ min}$$
Drinking started $2$ h $38$ min before 10:30 pm.
$$\therefore\ \text{Drinking started at } 7{:}52 \text{ pm.}$$
criteria: Substitutes into the $BAC$ formula, or equivalent merit
Finds the number of hours for $BAC$ to reach zero, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The formula $BAC_{\text{Female}} = \dfrac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M}$ gives the Blood Alcohol Content for females, where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours of drinking, and $M$ is the person's weight in kilograms.

Calculate the BAC for Emma, whose weight is 70 kg, and who consumed 5 standard drinks over a period of 4 hours.

solutions.latex:
Substitute $N=5$, $H=4$ and $M=70$ into the given formula.
$$\begin{aligned} BAC &= \dfrac{10\times 5-7.5\times 4}{5.5\times 70} \\ &= \dfrac{50-30}{385} \\ &= \dfrac{20}{385} \\ &\approx 0.052 \end{aligned}$$
So the BAC is $0.052$, which is option C.

parts.latex:
The formula below is used to calculate an estimate for the blood alcohol content (BAC) of males.

$$\text{BAC}_{male}=\dfrac{10N-7.5H}{6.8M}$$

where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours between the first and the last drink, and $M$ is the mass in kilograms.

Stephen weighs 98 kilograms. He consumed 6.5 standard drinks between 6:00 pm and 9:45 pm. He then stopped drinking alcohol.

His BAC reached zero at 1:15am. Calculate the rate at which his body metabolised the alcohol, in terms of BAC per hour. Give your answer correct to four decimal places.

solutions.latex:
Stephen drank from 6:00 pm to 9:45 pm, so $H=3.75$ hours.

Substitute into the formula with $N=6.5$ and $M=98$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{BAC}&=\dfrac{10\times 6.5-7.5\times 3.75}{6.8\times 98}\\&=0.0553346\ldots\end{aligned}$$
His BAC reached zero 3.5 hours after 9:45 pm (at 1:15 am).
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Rate of metabolism}&=\dfrac{\text{BAC}}{\text{time taken}}\\&=\dfrac{0.0553346\ldots}{3.5}\\&\approx 0.0158 \text{ BAC/hour (to 4 d.p.)}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Expresses the time spent drinking as a decimal, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Blood alcohol for a female can be estimated using the following BAC formula

$$\text{BAC}_{\text{Female}} = \dfrac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M} ,$$

where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours since they started drinking and $M$ is the person's mass in kilograms.

Georgia weighs 58 kg and had a BAC of 0.08 after drinking for 2 hours.

How many standard drinks did she have, to the nearest whole number?

solutions.latex:
Substitute $\text{BAC} = 0.08$, $H = 2$ and $M = 58$ into the formula.
$$\begin{aligned} 0.08 &= \dfrac{10N - 7.5(2)}{5.5(58)} \\ 0.08 &= \dfrac{10N - 15}{319} \\ 10N - 15 &= 25.52 \\ 10N &= 40.52 \\ N &= 4.052 \approx 4 \end{aligned}$$
Georgia had 4 standard drinks, so the answer is C.
